OracleUtils.ethToToken multiplies an already 18-decimal result by 10**(18 - decimals), over-scaling the returned token amount for sub-18-decimal assets so mint or credit paths over-pay.
column6: contracts/libraries/OracleUtils.sol:98 tokenAmount * 10 ** (18 - _decimals)

column5: OracleUtils.ethToTokenRoundUp applies the same wrong-direction 10**(18 - decimals) multiply to its rounded-up result, over-scaling the token amount for sub-18-decimal assets on the round-up leg.
column6: contracts/libraries/OracleUtils.sol:151 tokenAmount * 10 ** (18 - _decimals)

column5: OracleUtils.ethLeftSide infers feed orientation from only the first three bytes of the feed description, so an ETH-prefixed asset quoted in ETH is misclassified and every conversion takes the wrong mul/div leg, mispricing that asset for minters and redeemers.
column6: contracts/libraries/OracleUtils.sol:266 3-byte prefix compare against ETH

column5: The checkSequencerActive modifier has no startedAt == 0 check, so an uninitialized sequencer-uptime round makes block.timestamp - 0 exceed the grace period and prices are served during the window the grace check is meant to block.
